The answer is A. Spinal ependymomas often present with pain and gradual neurological deficit. Complete surgical resection is often curative.
questions.keyConcept: Adult ependymomas occur most often in the spinal cord; pediatric ependymomas occur in the fourth ventricle.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.text: Describe the gross pathology of Ependymomas.
questions.explanation: Ependymomas appear as: well-demarcated, grayish-red masses that may be solid or cystic. They may have areas of hemorrhage and necrosis. Intracranial ependymomas often fill the ventricle; spinal ependymomas are intramedullary. The answer is A. The well-circumscribed nature allows for surgical resection.
questions.keyConcept: Ependymomas are well-demarcated masses - intracranial tumors fill ventricles, spinal tumors are intramedullary.
options: Ependymomas are well-circumscribed tumors that are soft and spongy
Ependymomas are highly vascular with necrosis
Ependymomas are mucinous with myxoid stroma
Ependymomas are often cystic with a mural nodule

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.text: What are the microscopic features of Ependymomas?
questions.explanation: Ependymoma microscopic features include: perivascular pseudorosettes (tumor cells arranged around blood vessels with fibrillary processes) and true ependymal rosettes (tumor cells arranged around central lumen). The cells have uniform, round to oval nuclei. The answer is A. Perivascular pseudorosettes are the most distinctive feature. GFAP is positive.
questions.keyConcept: Ependymomas show perivascular pseudorosettes and true rosettes - diagnostic histological features.
options: Uniform small cells, round to oval nuclei with granular chromatin
Highly cellular with marked nuclear atypia

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which drugs are classified as opioid antitussives?
questions.explanation: Opioid antitussives include: codeine and dextromethorphan. These act on the cough center in the medulla. Codeine is a weak opioid agonist used for cough and pain. Dextromethorphan is a non-opioid that acts on sigma receptors and NMDA receptors.选项C正确. The answer is C. These are central cough suppressants.
questions.keyConcept: Codeine and dextromethorphan are opioid antitussives acting on the medullary cough center.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Name some strong pure agonists opioids.
questions.explanation: Strong pure agonist opioids include: morphine, heroin, fentanyl, methadone, meperidine, hydromorphone, oxymorphone.选项D正确. The answer is D. These have full agonist activity at mu opioid receptors, providing maximum analgesia but also respiratory depression, sedation, and dependence potential.
questions.keyConcept: Morphine, fentanyl, methadone are strong pure mu opioid agonists - maximum analgesia with respiratory depression risk.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What are the partial agonists opioids?
questions.explanation: Partial agonist opioids include buprenorphine (partial mu agonist) and pentazocine (partial kappa agonist, mixed agonist-antagonist).选项A正确. Buprenorphine is used for opioid dependence (Suboxone) and analgesia. Its ceiling effect on respiratory depression makes it safer. The answer is A. Pentazocine can precipitate withdrawal in opioid-dependent patients.
questions.keyConcept: Buprenorphine is a partial mu agonist with ceiling effect on respiratory depression - used in opioid dependence treatment.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What is the classification of codeine? And what’s it’s uses?
questions.explanation: Codeine is classified as a weak opioid agonist with moderate analgesic and antitussive effects. Uses: mild-moderate pain (often with acetaminophen or aspirin), cough suppression, and diarrhea treatment.选项A正确. The answer is A. Codeine's analgesic effect requires metabolic conversion to morphine by CYP2D6.
questions.keyConcept: Codeine is a weak opioid used for mild pain, cough, and diarrhea - requires CYP2D6 activation to morphine.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which drugs are classified as opioid antidiarrheals?
questions.explanation: Opioid antidiarrheals include: loperamide (Imodium), diphenoxylate (with atropine as Lomotil), and opium tincture. These act on mu receptors in the myenteric plexus, decreasing motility and secretion.选项C正确. The answer is C. Loperamide does not cross BBB significantly, avoiding CNS effects.
questions.keyConcept: Loperamide and diphenoxylate are opioid antidiarrheals - mu receptor agonists in the gut decreasing motility.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What is the cause of iatrogenic Parkinson’s disease?
questions.explanation: Iatrogenic Parkinson's disease is caused by drugs that block dopamine receptors: antipsychotics (haloperidol, chlorpromazine, risperidone), antiemetics (metoclopramide, prochlorperazine), and some calcium channel blockers.选项A正确. The answer is A. Drug-induced parkinsonism is reversible upon drug discontinuation but may take weeks to months.
questions.keyConcept: Dopamine-blocking drugs (antipsychotics, metoclopramide) cause iatrogenic parkinsonism - reversible upon discontinuation.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What is the aim of drug therapy in Parkinson’s disease?
questions.explanation: The aim of drug therapy in Parkinson's disease is to restore dopamine deficiency and reduce excess cholinergic activity. This involves: dopamine replacement (L-dopa, dopamine agonists), COMT inhibitors (entacapone), MAO-B inhibitors (selegiline), and anticholinergics for tremor.选项A正确. The answer is A. Treatment aims to improve motor symptoms and quality of life.
questions.keyConcept: PD drug therapy aims to restore dopaminergic activity and reduce cholinergic excess - improving motor function.
options: To restore balance between dopamine and acetylcholine activity in the basal ganglia
To increase dopamine activity in the basal ganglia
To decrease acetylcholine activity in the basal ganglia

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What is L-Dopa?
questions.explanation: L-Dopa is levodopa, the metabolic precursor of dopamine that crosses the blood-brain barrier. It is converted to dopamine by aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (DOPA decarboxylase) in the brain and periphery.选项A正确. The answer is A. L-dopa is combined with carbidopa (a peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor) to reduce peripheral side effects and increase CNS delivery.
questions.keyConcept: Levodopa is a dopamine precursor that crosses the BBB - converted to dopamine by DOPA decarboxylase in the brain.
options: A dopamine precursor that can cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB)

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: How is L-Dopa converted to dopamine?
questions.explanation: L-Dopa is converted to dopamine by aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (DOPA decarboxylase), also called DOPA decarboxylase. This enzyme requires pyridoxine (B6) as cofactor. The reaction occurs in the brain (after L-dopa crosses BBB) and in peripheral tissues.选项A正确. The answer is A. Carbidopa inhibits peripheral conversion, allowing more L-dopa to reach the brain.
questions.keyConcept: DOPA decarboxylase converts levodopa to dopamine - carbidopa inhibits this peripheral conversion.
options: L-Dopa is decarboxylated by the central dopa decarboxylase enzyme to dopamine (DA) in the dopaminergic neurons
L-Dopa is converted to dopamine by MAO-B
L-Dopa is converted to dopamine by COMT
L-Dopa is converted to dopamine by aldehyde dehydrogenase

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What are the therapeutic uses of anticholinergic drugs?
questions.explanation: Anticholinergic drugs therapeutic uses in PD: control of tremor and rigidity (not bradykinesia), drooling, excessive salivation, and oily skin. They work by blocking muscarinic receptors in the striatum, reducing cholinergic activity that becomes relatively increased in PD.选项C正确. The answer is C. Anticholinergics are less effective for bradykinesia and are now second-line due to side effects.
questions.keyConcept: Anticholinergics treat PD tremor and rigidity by blocking excess cholinergic activity in the striatum.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What are the side effects of anticholinergic drugs?
questions.explanation: Anticholinergic side effects include: dry mouth, blurred vision (cycloplegia), constipation, urinary retention, tachycardia, confusion, and memory impairment (especially in elderly). 'Blind as a bat, dry as a bone, red as a beet, mad as a hatter' describes these effects.选项D正确. The answer is D. Contraindicated in narrow-angle glaucoma, urinary retention, and benign prostatic hyperplasia.
questions.keyConcept: Anticholinergic side effects: dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation, urinary retention, confusion - 'dry as bone'.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What are the first choice agents in early Parkinson’s disease?
questions.explanation: First choice agents in early Parkinson's disease: levodopa/carbidopa combinations (most effective for motor symptoms) and dopamine agonists (ropinirole, pramipexole) as alternatives. MAO-B inhibitors (selegiline) may be used early.选项D正确. The answer is D. Treatment choice depends on age, symptom severity, and cognitive status.
questions.keyConcept: Levodopa/carbidopa and dopamine agonists are first-line for early PD - L-dopa is most effective, agonists delay motor complications.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What are the uses of Benzodiazepines?
questions.explanation: Benzodiazepine uses: anxiety disorders, insomnia, seizures (status epilepticus - diazepam, lorazepam), muscle spasms, alcohol withdrawal, sedation before procedures, and amnesia (midazolam).选项D正确. The answer is D. They enhance GABA-A receptor activity, increasing chloride conductance.
questions.keyConcept: Benzodiazepines treat anxiety, insomnia, seizures, muscle spasms, and alcohol withdrawal via GABA enhancement.
options: Secondary anxiety due to psychiatric disease

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: How do Benzodiazepines affect sleep?
questions.explanation: Benzodiazepines affect sleep by: decreasing sleep latency, increasing total sleep time, reducing REM sleep, increasing stage 2 sleep, and decreasing slow-wave sleep. They suppress REM and deep sleep, affecting sleep quality.选项D正确. The answer is D. This explains the groggy feeling and why they are not ideal for long-term sleep management.
questions.keyConcept: Benzodiazepines reduce REM and slow-wave sleep while increasing stage 2 - improving sleep onset but reducing quality.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What are the classifications of local anesthetics?
questions.explanation: Local anesthetics classified by: 1) Chemical structure - esters (procaine, tetracaine, benzocaine) and amides (lidocaine, bupivacaine, ropivacaine); 2) Duration of action - short, intermediate, long-acting.选项C正确. The answer is C. Esters are metabolized by plasma cholinesterase; amides are metabolized in liver.
questions.keyConcept: Local anesthetics are classified as esters vs amides (metabolism) and by duration of action (short/intermediate/long).

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Why are vasoconstrictors added to local anesthetics?
questions.explanation: Vasoconstrictors (epinephrine, norepinephrine, felypressin) are added to local anesthetics to: constrict blood vessels, reduce bleeding, decrease systemic absorption, prolong anesthetic duration, and reduce peak plasma levels.选项C正确. The answer is C. Contraindicated in patients with cardiovascular disease, hyperthyroidism, and those on non-selective beta-blockers.
questions.keyConcept: Vasoconstrictors prolong local anesthetic duration and reduce toxicity by decreasing systemic absorption and bleeding.
options: To prolong the duration of action
To reduce systemic adverse effects and bleeding tendency

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: How do general anesthetics inhibit neuronal activity?
questions.explanation: General anesthetics inhibit neuronal activity by enhancing inhibitory neurotransmission (GABA-A receptor activation - barbiturates, benzodiazepines, propofol, isoflurane) or inhibiting excitatory neurotransmission (NMDA receptor blockade - ketamine, nitrous oxide).选项C正确. The answer is C. Some agents do both. The net effect is decreased neuronal excitability and consciousness.
questions.keyConcept: General anesthetics enhance GABA (inhibitory) or block NMDA (excitatory) to inhibit neuronal activity.
options: They facilitate inhibitory effects of GABA at GABA receptors
Inhibit excitatory effects of glutamate at NMDA receptors

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What are the classic antiepileptic drugs?
questions.explanation: Classic antiepileptic drugs include: phenytoin, carbamazepine, valproic acid, ethosuximide, phenobarbital, and benzodiazepines. These are first-generation drugs with well-established efficacy.选项D正确. The answer is D. They have more drug interactions and side effects compared to newer agents.
questions.keyConcept: Phenytoin, carbamazepine, valproate, ethosuximide are classic antiepileptics - more side effects and interactions than newer drugs.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What are the newer antiepileptic drugs?
questions.explanation: Newer antiepileptic drugs include: lamotrigine, levetiracetam, topiramate, gabapentin, pregabalin, vigabatrin, tiagabine, oxcarbazepine, lacosamide, and zonimide. These have improved side effect profiles.选项D正确. The answer is D. They are often used as adjuncts or alternatives to classic drugs.
questions.keyConcept: Lamotrigine, levetiracetam, topiramate are newer antiepileptics - better tolerated with fewer drug interactions.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What drugs are used to terminate acute migraine attacks?
questions.explanation: Drugs to terminate acute migraine attacks: triptans (sumatriptan, rizatriptan), ergotamines, NSAIDs, acetaminophen, antiemetics (metoclopramide), and combination analgesics.选项D正确. The answer is D. Triptans are most effective; ergotamines are for moderate attacks. Prophylaxis uses beta-blockers, TCAs, anticonvulsants.
questions.keyConcept: Acute migraine: triptans, ergotamines, NSAIDs - treat attack; prophylaxis uses beta-blockers, TCAs, topiramate.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What is the mechanism of action of antidepressants?
questions.explanation: Antidepressants work mainly by increasing synaptic monoamine levels (serotonin, norepinephrine, dopamine). SSRIs inhibit serotonin reuptake; SNRIs inhibit both; TCAs inhibit norepinephrine and serotonin; MAOIs inhibit monoamine oxidase.选项C正确. The answer is C. The monoamine hypothesis suggests depression involves decreased serotonin/norepinephrine.
questions.keyConcept: Antidepressants increase synaptic monoamines (serotonin, norepinephrine) via reuptake inhibition or enzyme blockade.
options: Increase brain biogenic amines (norepinephrine and serotonin)

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which class of antidepressants is reserved for atypical depression associated with anxiety and phobia?
questions.explanation: MAO inhibitors (MAOIs) like phenelzine, tranylcypromine are reserved for atypical depression associated with hypersomnia, hyperphagia, and mood reactivity.选项A正确. The answer is A. They require dietary restrictions (tyramine avoidance) due to hypertensive crisis risk.
questions.keyConcept: MAOIs are reserved for atypical depression with hypersomnia and hyperphagia - require tyramine dietary restrictions.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which class of antidepressants is the first choice for initial therapy?
questions.explanation: SSRIs (fluoxetine, sertraline, paroxetine, citalopram, escitalopram) are first-choice for initial therapy due to: efficacy, once-daily dosing, safety in overdose, and favorable side effect profile.选项B正确. The answer is B. They are better tolerated than TCAs and MAOIs.
questions.keyConcept: SSRIs are first-line antidepressants - safe, effective, once-daily, and favorable side effect profile.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which class of antidepressants is reserved for resistant cases?
questions.explanation: MAOI antidepressants are reserved for resistant cases that fail other antidepressants. They require careful monitoring and dietary restrictions.选项C正确. The answer is C. They are used when SSRIs, SNRIs, and TCAs have failed due to their complexity and risk.
questions.keyConcept: MAOIs are reserved for treatment-resistant depression - require tyramine diet and careful monitoring.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: How is Drug Induced Aseptic Meningitis treated?
questions.explanation: Drug-induced aseptic meningitis (DIAM) is treated by: discontinuing the offending drug, supportive care, and sometimes corticosteroids. Common culprits: NSAIDs, antibiotics (sulfonamides, penicillins), IVIG.选项A正确. The answer is A. Symptoms resolve with drug discontinuation. CSF shows lymphocytic pleocytosis.
questions.keyConcept: Drug-induced aseptic meningitis is treated by discontinuing the causative drug - NSAIDs, antibiotics, IVIG are common triggers.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which antibiotics achieve therapeutic CSF level even without meningeal inflammation?
questions.explanation: Antibiotics achieving therapeutic CSF levels WITHOUT meningeal inflammation: sulfonamides, fluoroquinolones, and some others. These can cross normal blood-brain barrier.选项A正确. The answer is A. Most antibiotics require meningeal inflammation for adequate CSF penetration.
questions.keyConcept: Sulfonamides and fluoroquinolones achieve CSF levels without meningeal inflammation - unique BBB penetration.
options: Aminoglycosides, 1st & 2nd Generation of cephalosporines, Amphotericin B

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which antibiotics achieve therapeutic CSF level only with meningeal inflammation?
questions.explanation: Antibiotics achieving therapeutic CSF levels ONLY with meningeal inflammation: penicillins, cephalosporins, vancomycin, aminoglycosides, and most others.选项B正确. The answer is B. Meningeal inflammation increases BBB permeability, allowing these antibiotics to penetrate.
questions.keyConcept: Most antibiotics (penicillins, cephalosporins, vancomycin) require meningeal inflammation for adequate CSF penetration.
options: Aminoglycosides, 1st & 2nd Generation of cephalosporines, Amphotericin B

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which antibiotics do not achieve therapeutic CSF level even with inflammation?
questions.explanation: Antibiotics NOT achieving therapeutic CSF even with inflammation: aminoglycosides (gentamicin, streptomycin), amphotericin B, and others with poor CNS penetration.选项A正确. Most drugs require meningeal inflammation for penetration, but some never achieve adequate levels. The answer is A. This is why intrathecal administration is needed for some infections.
questions.keyConcept: Aminoglycosides and amphotericin B do not achieve therapeutic CSF levels even with meningeal inflammation.
options: Aminoglycosides, 1st & 2nd Generation of cephalosporines, Amphotericin B

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What is the initial management for bacterial meningitis?
questions.explanation: Initial management of bacterial meningitis: immediate blood cultures, then empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics (3rd gen cephalosporin + vancomycin + ampicillin if >50yo/immunocompromised), plus dexamethasone before or with first antibiotic dose.选项A正确. Lumbar puncture follows if no contraindications. The answer is A. Every hour of delay increases mortality.
questions.keyConcept: Bacterial meningitis requires immediate empiric antibiotics (3rd gen cephalosporin + vancomycin) and dexamethasone.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What is the aim of dexamethasone therapy in meningitis?
questions.explanation: Dexamethasone in meningitis reduces inflammation and cerebral edema, lowering intracranial pressure. It decreases neurological complications and mortality, especially in pneumococcal meningitis.选项A正确. Give BEFORE or with first antibiotic dose. The answer is A. Steroids reduce the inflammatory response to bacterial lysis.
questions.keyConcept: Dexamethasone reduces cerebral inflammation and complications in bacterial meningitis when given early.
options: Improve outcome by reducing inflammation-induced brain edema and complications

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What antibiotics are used for empirical therapy in suspected bacterial meningitis in a one month case?
questions.explanation: Empirical therapy for bacterial meningitis: 3rd generation cephalosporin (ceftriaxone or cefotaxime) PLUS vancomycin (for resistant pneumococcus). In patients >50 or immunocompromised, add ampicillin for Listeria.选项A正确. The answer is A. Therapy is adjusted once culture and sensitivity return.
questions.keyConcept: Empiric bacterial meningitis therapy: 3rd gen cephalosporin + vancomycin ± ampicillin for Listeria coverage.
options: Aminoglycosides, 1st & 2nd Generation of cephalosporines, Amphotericin B

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What antibiotics are used in intrathecal injection for nosocomial meningitis?
questions.explanation: Antibiotics used intrathecally for nosocomial meningitis: vancomycin and aminoglycosides (gentamicin, amikacin). These achieve high local concentrations.选项A正确. The answer is A. Intrathecal use bypasses BBB limitations.
questions.keyConcept: Vancomycin and aminoglycosides are given intrathecally for nosocomial meningitis to achieve high CSF levels.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What antibiotics should be avoided in intrathecal injection for meningitis?
questions.explanation: Antibiotics to AVOID intrathecally: penicillins (can cause seizures), chloramphenicol (can cause 'grey baby' syndrome), and others.选项A正确. The answer is A. Only vancomycin, aminoglycosides, and occasionally others are safe intrathecally.
questions.keyConcept: Penicillins and chloramphenicol should be avoided intrathecally due to neurotoxicity risk.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What is the choice of antibiotic in bacterial meningitis for patients <1 month?
questions.explanation: Bacterial meningitis in patients <1 month: Ampicillin + Cefotaxime (or aminoglycoside). Covers Group B Strep, E. coli, Listeria.选项B正确. The answer is B. Age-specific empiric therapy covers the most likely pathogens for that age group.
questions.keyConcept: Neonatal meningitis (<1 month): ampicillin + cefotaxime - covers Group B Strep, E. coli, Listeria.
options: Aminoglycosides, 1st & 2nd Generation of cephalosporines, Amphotericin B

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What is the triple therapy for cases with patients > 50 years or immunocompromised?
questions.explanation: Triple therapy for patients >50 years or immunocompromised: Ampicillin + 3rd gen cephalosporin + Vancomycin. Adds Listeria and resistant pneumococcus coverage.选项A正确. The answer is A. Immunocompromised patients need broader coverage.
questions.keyConcept: Elderly/immunocompromised meningitis: ampicillin + 3rd gen cephalosporin + vancomycin triple therapy.
options: Aminoglycosides, 1st & 2nd Generation of cephalosporines, Amphotericin B

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which antibiotic is used in all cases of bacterial meningitis except in children < 1 month?
questions.explanation: 3rd generation cephalosporins (ceftriaxone, cefotaxime) are used in ALL cases of bacterial meningitis EXCEPT in neonates (<1 month) where ampicillin-based regimens are used.选项A正确. The answer is A. Ceftriaxone is the cornerstone of empiric bacterial meningitis therapy.
questions.keyConcept: 3rd generation cephalosporins are universal bacterial meningitis coverage except in neonates requiring ampicillin.
options: Aminoglycosides, 1st & 2nd Generation of cephalosporines, Amphotericin B

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What is the empirical therapy for bacterial meningitis in children < 1 month?
questions.explanation: Empirical therapy for neonatal bacterial meningitis (<1 month): Ampicillin + Cefotaxime (or Gentamicin). Covers Group B Strep, E. coli, Listeria, and other neonate pathogens.选项A正确. The answer is A. Duration is typically 2-3 weeks depending on organism.
questions.keyConcept: Neonatal meningitis: ampicillin + cefotaxime covers the key neonate pathogens including Group B Strep.
options: Aminoglycosides, 1st & 2nd Generation of cephalosporines, Amphotericin B

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: Which antibiotic is used in all cases of bacterial meningitis except in surgical interference in the brain?
questions.explanation: 3rd generation cephalosporins are used in ALL bacterial meningitis EXCEPT post-neurosurgical meningitis, where Pseudomonas-coverage (cefepime, meropenem) is needed.选项A正确. The answer is A. Post-surgical patients need different empiric coverage for hospital-acquired pathogens.
questions.keyConcept: Post-surgical meningitis requires anti-pseudomonal coverage (cefepime, meropenem) instead of standard cephalosporins.
options: Aminoglycosides, 1st & 2nd Generation of cephalosporines, Amphotericin B

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What is the aim of management for Alzheimer disease?
questions.explanation: Alzheimer's management aims to: slow cognitive decline, manage behavioral symptoms, improve quality of life, and support caregivers. Options include cholinesterase inhibitors, memantine, and behavioral interventions.选项C正确. The answer is C. There is no cure - treatment is symptomatic.
questions.keyConcept: Alzheimer's treatment aims to slow progression and manage symptoms - cholinesterase inhibitors and memantine are mainstays.
options: Increase cholinergic activity in the brain
Reduce excitotoxicity action of overstimulation of NMDA receptors

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What are the cholinesterase enzyme inhibitors used in the treatment of Alzheimer disease?
questions.explanation: Cholinesterase inhibitors for Alzheimer's: donepezil (Aricept), rivastigmine (Exelon), galantamine (Razadyne). These increase acetylcholine in the brain.选项D正确. The answer is D. They provide modest symptomatic benefit.
questions.keyConcept: Donepezil, rivastigmine, galantamine are cholinesterase inhibitors - modestly effective in Alzheimer's.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What is the mechanism of action of cholinesterase enzyme inhibitors?
questions.explanation: Cholinesterase inhibitors work by blocking acetylcholinesterase, preventing breakdown of acetylcholine. This increases synaptic ACh levels, compensating for cholinergic neuron loss.选项A正确. The answer is A. They don't cure disease but slow symptom progression.
questions.keyConcept: Cholinesterase inhibitors increase brain acetylcholine by blocking its breakdown - compensating for cholinergic loss.
options: Inhibits Acetylcholine esterase > increases cholinergic transmission in the brain

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What is the mechanism of action of memantine?
questions.explanation: Memantine is an NMDA receptor antagonist that blocks glutamate excitotoxicity. It provides neuroprotection by preventing calcium-mediated neuronal damage.选项A正确. The answer is A. Used in moderate-severe Alzheimer's, often with cholinesterase inhibitor.
questions.keyConcept: Memantine blocks NMDA receptors to prevent glutamate excitotoxicity - neuroprotective in Alzheimer's.
options: Noncompetitive NMDA receptor antagonist and protects neurons from glutamate induced excitotoxicity
Blocks presynaptic voltage gated Na+ channels

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What is Namzaric?
questions.explanation: Namzaric is a combination of donepezil (cholinesterase inhibitor) and memantine (NMDA antagonist) in a single capsule. It simplifies regimen for moderate-severe Alzheimer's.选项A正确. The answer is A. Combination therapy targets both cholinergic and glutamatergic systems.
questions.keyConcept: Namzaric combines donepezil + memantine for dual action in moderate-severe Alzheimer's.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What is the management approach for Multiple Sclerosis?
questions.explanation: MS management: disease-modifying therapies (interferon-beta, glatiramer, natalizumab, fingolimod) for relapsing forms; symptom management; rehabilitation.选项D正确. The answer is D. No cure - treatment aims to reduce relapses and disability.
questions.keyConcept: MS management uses disease-modifying therapies to reduce relapse rate and slow disability progression.
options: Treatment of acute episodes (exacerbations) with corticosteroids

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What is the treatment for an acute episode (exacerbation) of MS?
questions.explanation: Acute MS exacerbation treatment: high-dose IV methylprednisolone (500mg-1g/day for 3-5 days). This speeds recovery from relapse but doesn't alter long-term course.选项C正确. The answer is C. Plasma exchange may be used for steroid-refractory relapses.
questions.keyConcept: MS acute exacerbations are treated with high-dose IV corticosteroids - plasma exchange for refractory cases.
options: Methyl prednisolone: 1 gm/day for 5 days IV
followed by oral prednisone with gradual decrease

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What are the first-line therapy drugs used in the treatment of MS?
questions.explanation: First-line MS disease-modifying drugs: interferon-beta preparations (Avonex, Betaseron, Rebif), glatiramer acetate (Copaxone). These reduce relapse rate by ~30%.选项A正确. The answer is A. They are injectables with modest efficacy.
questions.keyConcept: Interferon-beta and glatiramer are first-line MS disease-modifying therapies - reduce relapse rate ~30%.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What is the mechanism of action of typical antipsychotics?
questions.explanation: Typical antipsychotics (haloperidol, chlorpromazine) work by blocking D2 dopamine receptors, reducing dopaminergic transmission in mesolimbic pathway (treats positive symptoms).选项A正确. The answer is A. Also blocks D2 in nigrostriatal pathway (causes EPS) and tuberoinfundibular pathway (hyperprolactinemia).
questions.keyConcept: Typical antipsychotics block D2 receptors - therapeutic for psychosis but cause EPS and hyperprolactinemia.
options: Blocking D2 receptors in the mesolimbic system improves positive symptoms

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What receptors do atypical antipsychotics block in addition to D2 receptors?
questions.explanation: Atypical antipsychotics (clozapine, olanzapine, risperidone) block D2 plus serotonin 5-HT2A receptors. This 5-HT2A blockade allows more dopamine in nigrostriatal pathway, reducing EPS.选项A正确. The answer is A. This dual blockade gives atypicals their improved side effect profile.
questions.keyConcept: Atypical antipsychotics block both D2 and 5-HT2A receptors - greater dopamine in motor pathways reduces EPS.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What are the typical antipsychotics?
questions.explanation: Typical antipsychotics include: haloperidol, chlorpromazine, thioridazine, fluphenazine, perphenazine, and flupentixol.选项D正确. The answer is D. They have high D2 affinity and significant EPS risk.
questions.keyConcept: Haloperidol, chlorpromazine, thioridazine are typical antipsychotics - high EPS risk from D2 blockade.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What are the atypical antipsychotics?
questions.explanation: Atypical antipsychotics include: clozapine, olanzapine, risperidone, quetiapine, ziprasidone, aripiprazole, paliperidone.选项D正确. The answer is D. They have lower EPS risk but metabolic side effects.
questions.keyConcept: Clozapine, olanzapine, risperidone are atypicals - lower EPS but weight gain, metabolic syndrome risk.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What are the extrapyramidal adverse effects of antipsychotics?
questions.explanation: Extrapyramidal effects of antipsychotics: acute dystonia, akathisia (restlessness), parkinsonism (bradykinesia, rigidity, tremor), and tardive dyskinesia (late-onset choreiform movements).选项D正确. The answer is D. Caused by D2 blockade in nigrostriatal pathway.
questions.keyConcept: EPS includes acute dystonia, akathisia, parkinsonism, and tardive dyskinesia from nigrostriatal D2 blockade.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: How is bipolar manic depression managed during the euthymic period?
questions.explanation: Bipolar disorder euthymic (stable) period management: mood stabilizers (lithium, valproate, lamotrigine, carbamazepine) as maintenance therapy to prevent relapse.选项A正确. The answer is A. Lithium is gold standard for maintenance.
questions.keyConcept: Bipolar maintenance: lithium or mood stabilizers prevent relapse - lithium has best evidence for prophylaxis.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: How is bipolar manic depression managed during the manic period?
questions.explanation: Bipolar manic episode management: mood stabilizers (lithium, valproate) plus atypical antipsychotics (olanzapine, quetiapine, risperidone). Option A正确. The answer is A. ECT for severe/refractory cases. Lithium takes weeks to work.
questions.keyConcept: Acute mania: mood stabilizer + atypical antipsychotic; lithium effective but slow onset.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What are the indications of lithium?
questions.explanation: Lithium indications: bipolar disorder (acute mania and maintenance), major depression (augmentation), and cluster headache prophylaxis.选项D正确. The answer is D. Requires regular level monitoring (narrow therapeutic index).
questions.keyConcept: Lithium treats bipolar disorder, treatment-resistant depression, and cluster headache - narrow therapeutic window.
options: Adjunct to antidepressants in refractory depression

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What are the risks of chronic abuse of opioids?
questions.explanation: Chronic opioid abuse risks: respiratory depression, dependence/addiction, constipation, hormonal dysfunction (hypogonadism), hyperalgesia, and infections (HIV, hepatitis from IV use).选项D正确. The answer is D. Opioid tolerance develops, requiring higher doses.
questions.keyConcept: Chronic opioid abuse causes respiratory depression, dependence, constipation, hormonal dysfunction, and infection risk.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: How is opioid abuse managed?
questions.explanation: Opioid abuse management: detoxification (methadone, buprenorphine maintenance), behavioral therapy, naltrexone (opioid antagonist) to prevent relapse, and support groups.选项D正确. The answer is D. Methadone maintenance is gold standard for opioid dependence.
questions.keyConcept: Opioid dependence: methadone/buprenorphine maintenance, naltrexone, behavioral therapy - comprehensive approach.

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What is the mechanism of nicotine addiction?
questions.explanation: Nicotine addiction mechanism: nicotine binds nicotinic acetylcholine receptors in VTA, causing dopamine release in nucleus accumbens (reward pathway). This creates positive reinforcement.选项A正确. The answer is A. Dopamine release produces the 'buzz' and craving.
questions.keyConcept: Nicotine activates VTA nicotinic receptors → dopamine release in reward pathway → addiction.
options: Stimulates nicotinic Ach receptors in VTA leading to dopamine release in reward pathway
Blocks nicotinic Ach receptors in VTA
Increases serotonin levels in the brain
Decreases dopamine levels in the brain

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What are the symptoms of nicotine withdrawal syndrome?
questions.explanation: Nicotine withdrawal symptoms: irritability, anxiety, difficulty concentrating, increased appetite, insomnia, depressed mood, and intense craving for nicotine.选项A正确. The answer is A. Symptoms peak within first week, subside over 2-4 weeks.
questions.keyConcept: Nicotine withdrawal: irritability, insomnia, increased appetite, depression, craving - peaks first week.
options: Insomnia, anxiety, aggressiveness, and increased appetite
Drowsiness, calmness, and decreased heart rate
Increased energy, alertness, and improved mood

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: What is the mechanism of action of Varenicline?
questions.explanation: Varenicline (Chantix) is a partial agonist at alpha4-beta2 nicotinic receptors. It reduces nicotine craving by partial activation and prevents nicotine reward by blocking full agonist effects.选项A正确. The answer is A. FDA-approved for smoking cessation.
questions.keyConcept: Varenicline partial agonism at nicotinic receptors reduces craving while blocking nicotine effects.
options: Block the ability of nicotine to stimulate dopamine system in VTA
Stimulate nicotinic Ach receptors in VTA leading to dopamine release
Increase serotonin levels in the brain
Decrease dopamine levels in the brain

questions.subject: Pharmacology
questions.text: How is nicotine abuse managed?
questions.explanation: Nicotine abuse management: nicotine replacement therapy (patches, gum, lozenges, inhaler), varenicline, bupropion, counseling.选项D正确. The answer is D. Combination of pharmacotherapy and behavioral support is most effective.
questions.keyConcept: Smoking cessation: NRT, varenicline, bupropion plus counseling - combination is most effective.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: What are the characteristics of proteolytic strains?
questions.explanation: Proteolytic strains characteristics: produce enzymes that degrade tissue, cause more invasive/necrotizing infections.选项D正确. The answer is D. Associated with severe infections and tissue destruction.
questions.keyConcept: Proteolytic bacterial strains degrade tissue proteins, causing invasive, necrotizing infections.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: What are the clinical manifestations of Tetanus?
questions.explanation: Tetanus clinical manifestations: lockjaw (trismus), risus sardonicus, opisthotonus, muscle rigidity, spasms triggered by stimuli, and autonomic dysfunction.选项D正确. The answer is D. Spasms can cause fractures. Incubation: 3-21 days.
questions.keyConcept: Tetanus: lockjaw, risus sardonicus, opisthotonus, spasms - caused by tetanospasmin toxin.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: How can the presence of toxin be detected in botulism?
questions.explanation: Botulinum toxin detection: mouse bioassay (inoculate patient serum/feces into mice - death indicates toxin), PCR for organism, culture.选项D正确. The answer is D. Toxin blocks acetylcholine release at neuromuscular junction.
questions.keyConcept: Botulism diagnosis: mouse bioassay detects toxin - blocks ACh release causing flaccid paralysis.
options: In patient blood or food remnants using PCR or ELISA
Isolation of Clostridium botulinum from food

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: What are the classic symptoms of meningeal irritation?
questions.explanation: Classic meningeal irritation signs: neck stiffness (nuchal rigidity), positive Kernig sign (knee extension limited with hip flexed), positive Brudzinski sign (hip flexion with neck flexion).选项D正确. The answer is D. These indicate meningeal inflammation.
questions.keyConcept: Meningeal irritation: Kernig and Brudzinski signs - neck stiffness with characteristic reflex responses.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: What is the diagnostic test for meningitis?
questions.explanation: Diagnostic test for meningitis: lumbar puncture with CSF analysis (cell count, protein, glucose, Gram stain, culture, PCR).选项A正确. The answer is A. CSF shows: bacteria (neutrophils, high protein, low glucose), viral (lymphocytes, normal glucose).
questions.keyConcept: Lumbar puncture for CSF analysis - the definitive diagnostic test for meningitis.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: What are the members of the Herpesviridae family that can cause viral meningitis?
questions.explanation: Herpesviridae causing viral meningitis: HSV-1, HSV-2 (genital herpes), VZV, EBV, HHV-6.选项C正确. The answer is C. HSV-2 is a common cause of recurrent lymphocytic meningitis.
questions.keyConcept: HSV-2, HSV-1, VZV, EBV are Herpesviridae family members causing viral meningitis.

questions.subject: Microbiology
questions.text: What are the risk factors for rhinocerebral mucormycosis?
questions.explanation: Risk factors for rhinocerebral mucormycosis: uncontrolled diabetes (especially DKA), immunocompromise (neutropenia, steroids), iron overload, trauma/burns, and ketoacidosis.选项C正确. The answer is C. Diabetic patients are at highest risk.
questions.keyConcept: Rhinocerebral mucormycosis: uncontrolled diabetes and immunocompromise are main risk factors.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Pain from ala of nose is carried by which nerve?
questions.explanation: Pain from ala of nose carried by infratrochlear nerve (branch of V1 ophthalmic division of trigeminal).选项C正确. The answer is C. This nerve supplies the upper aspect of the nose including ala.
questions.keyConcept: Infratrochlear nerve (V1) carries sensation from the ala of the nose.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Regarding the scalp, the following statements are true Except:
questions.explanation: The scalp has 5 layers (SCALP): Skin, Connective tissue, Aponeurosis, Loose areolar tissue, Pericranium. The main blood vessels run in the connective tissue layer.选项E正确. The answer is E. The 'dangerous area' is the loose areolar tissue connecting to intracranial venous sinuses.
questions.keyConcept: Scalp layers (SCALP): skin, connective tissue, aponeurosis, loose areolar tissue, pericranium - vessels in layer 2.
options: Infection from scalp wounds can spread to superior sagittal sinus.
Its blood vessels run in the loose subaponeurotic space.
Its skin, superficial fascia, and aponeurosis move as one layer.
Frontal bellies of occipito-frontalis can corrugate skin of forehead.
Occipital bellies are supplied by facial nerve.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The large blood vessels of the scalp run into:
questions.explanation: The large blood vessels of the scalp run in the connective tissue layer (layer 2), between the skin and aponeurosis. They anastomose extensively.选项D正确. The answer is D. This layer is vascular and causes profuse bleeding when cut.
questions.keyConcept: Scalp blood vessels run in the subcutaneous connective tissue layer - profuse bleeding when injured.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Which of the following veins unite with a posterior branch of the retromandibular vein to form the external jugular vein?
questions.explanation: The retromandibular vein unites with the posterior auricular vein to form the external jugular vein.选项A正确. The answer is A. The external jugular drains the face and scalp.
questions.keyConcept: Retromandibular vein + posterior auricular vein = external jugular vein.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The plane of movement of the scalp is between:
questions.explanation: The plane of movement of the scalp is between the aponeurosis and pericranium (the loose areolar tissue layer). This allows scalp movement.选项B正确. The answer is B. Infection can spread in this 'dangerous layer' to intracranial structures.
questions.keyConcept: Scalp movement occurs between aponeurosis and pericranium - the loose areolar 'dangerous' layer.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Which of the following nerves supplying the scalp and face is not derived from the trigeminal nerve?
questions.explanation: The greater occipital nerve (C2) is NOT derived from the trigeminal nerve - it's a dorsal ramus of C2.选项A正确. The answer is A. It supplies the scalp posterior to the auricle.
questions.keyConcept: Greater occipital nerve (C2 dorsal ramus) is the only scalp nerve not from trigeminal - supplies posterior scalp.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Loss of sensation from the lower eyelid indicates injury of which nerve?
questions.explanation: Loss of sensation from lower eyelid indicates injury of infraorbital nerve (branch of V2 maxillary division of trigeminal).选项B正确. The answer is B. This nerve exits via infraorbital foramen.
questions.keyConcept: Infraorbital nerve (V2) supplies the lower eyelid - injury causes sensory loss in that distribution.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Which of the following muscles can produce transverse wrinkles in the forehead?
questions.explanation: The frontalis muscle (assisted by procerus and corrugator supercilii) can produce transverse wrinkles in the forehead when contracting.选项A正确. The answer is A. Frontalis is innervated by temporal branches of facial nerve.
questions.keyConcept: Frontalis muscle produces transverse forehead wrinkles - facial nerve (temporal branch) innervates it.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Retromandibular vein:
questions.explanation: Retromandibular vein is formed by union of maxillary and superficial temporal veins, lies deep to facial nerve in parotid gland, divides into anterior/posterior branches.选项E正确. The answer is E. It drains into external jugular vein.
questions.keyConcept: Retromandibular vein: formed by maxillary + superficial temporal veins; lies deep to facial nerve in parotid.
options: Is formed by the union of maxillary & superficial temporal veins.
Is deep to the facial nerve inside the parotid gland.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Bleeding beneath the pericranium of the scalp:
questions.explanation: Bleeding beneath the pericranium (subperiosteal hematoma) is LIMITED because pericranium is firmly attached to skull bones - it doesn't spread like the loose areolar layer.选项A正确. The answer is A. In contrast, bleeding in loose areolar layer is diffuse.
questions.keyConcept: Subperiosteal hematoma is localized - pericranium is firmly attached to bone unlike loose areolar layer.
options: Spreads underneath all of the scalp.
Makes a swelling that takes the shape of the underlying bone.
Reaches to the back of neck.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The motor nerve of the scalp behind the auricle is:
questions.explanation: The motor nerve of the scalp behind the auricle is the posterior auricular branch of facial nerve.选项B正确. The answer is B. It innervates posterior auricular and occipital muscles.
questions.keyConcept: Posterior auricular branch of facial nerve supplies muscles behind the auricle - motor to that area.
options: Posterior auricular branch of facial nerve.
Marginal mandibular branch of facial nerve.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Buccinator:
questions.explanation: Buccinator muscle: forms the cheek, keeps food between teeth during chewing, is pierced by parotid duct (Stensen's duct), and is innervated by facial nerve (buccal branch).选项C正确. The answer is C. It acts to blow, whistle, and chew.
questions.keyConcept: Buccinator: cheek muscle pierced by parotid duct, facial nerve innervation, keeps food between teeth.
options: Is one of the muscles of mastication.
Is supplied by buccal branch of mandibular nerve.
Arises from both mandible and maxilla.
Is covered by investing layer of fascia.
Accumulates food in vestibule of mouth.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Internal carotid artery supplies:
questions.explanation: Internal carotid artery supplies: brain, eye, forehead, and nose. It gives off ophthalmic artery (supplies eye), and anterior/middle cerebral arteries.选项A正确. The answer is A. It's the main supply to the brain.
questions.keyConcept: Internal carotid artery supplies the brain (cerebral hemispheres), eye, forehead - NOT the cheek or chin.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The upper lip:
questions.explanation: The upper lip: receives sensory innervation from infraorbital nerve (V2), motor from facial nerve, and lymph drains to submandibular nodes.选项E正确. The answer is E. The philtrum is midline - upper lip sensation is infraorbital.
questions.keyConcept: Upper lip: infraorbital nerve (V2) sensation, facial nerve motor, submandibular lymph drainage.
options: Lies in the dangerous area of face.
Its philtrum is obliterated in infections.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Which of the following contains parasympathetic postganglionic fibers?
questions.explanation: The pterygopalatine ganglion contains parasympathetic postganglionic fibers (from greater petrosal nerve and nerve of pterygoid canal).选项A正确. The answer is A. It relays parasympathetic to lacrimal, nasal, palatine glands.
questions.keyConcept: Pterygopalatine ganglion: parasympathetic postganglionic fibers - lacrimal, nasal, palatine secretion.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Pulse felt at antero-inferior angle of masseter is from which artery?
questions.explanation: Pulse felt at antero-inferior angle of masseter is from the facial artery - it crosses over the mandible at this point.选项D正确. The answer is D. This is where facial artery pulse can be palpated.
questions.keyConcept: Facial artery pulse is palpable at antero-inferior angle of masseter - crosses mandible there.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Lymph from central part of upper lip drains directly to:
questions.explanation: Lymph from central part of upper lip drains directly to submental lymph nodes (central group).选项B正确. The answer is B. Submental nodes drain the central lower face and lip.
questions.keyConcept: Central upper lip drains to submental nodes - important for lip cancer spread.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The branch of the mandibular nerve that supplies the scalp is the:
questions.explanation: The auriculotemporal nerve (branch of V3 mandibular division) supplies the scalp - specifically the temple region.选项E正确. The answer is E. It carries sensory info and parasympathetic to parotid.
questions.keyConcept: Auriculotemporal nerve (V3) supplies the scalp/side of head - auricle and temple region.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The scalp is:
questions.explanation: The scalp is: 5 layers (SCALP), highly vascular, innervated by multiple nerves, and the danger lies in the loose areolar layer connecting to intracranial sinuses.选项C正确. The answer is C. Infection can spread to meninges via this layer.
questions.keyConcept: Scalp has 5 layers - loose areolar tissue is the 'dangerous' layer connecting to intracranial venous sinuses.
options: Supplied by the great auricular nerve in front of the auricle.
Supplied by the supratrochlear and supraorbital arteries branches of the facial artery.
Supplied posteriorly by the greater occipital nerve from the ventral ramus of C2.
Supplied behind the auricle by the lesser occipital nerve from the ventral ramus of C2.
Drained by supratrochlear and supraorbital veins, which unite to form the superior ophthalmic vein.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Facial artery:
questions.explanation: Facial artery: branch of external carotid, tortuous course, enters face at antero-inferior angle of buccinator, ends at side of nose (angular artery).选项C正确. The answer is C. It's the main arterial supply to the face.
questions.keyConcept: Facial artery: external carotid branch, tortuous, supplies face - enters at buccinator angle, ends at nose.
options: Is a branch of internal carotid artery
Enters face at antero-inferior angle of Buccinator
Ends by anastomosing with supraorbital artery.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The nerve supply of the muscle of the scalp is:
questions.explanation: The nerve supply of scalp muscles (including frontalis, occipitalis) is via facial nerve branches - temporal, posterior auricular, and other branches.选项D正确. The answer is D. Sensory innervation is via trigeminal branches.
questions.keyConcept: Motor to scalp muscles: facial nerve (temporal and posterior auricular branches) - sensory: trigeminal branches.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Infection from dangerous area of face may be transmitted to the following venous sinus:
questions.explanation: Infection from dangerous area of face (upper lip, nose, orbit) may spread via facial vein → angular vein → superior ophthalmic vein → cavernous sinus.选项E正确. The answer is E. This is why facial infections can cause cavernous sinus thrombosis.
questions.keyConcept: Facial vein connects to cavernous sinus via angular and superior ophthalmic veins - spread route for infection.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The lowermost soft part of the auricle of ear is called:
questions.explanation: The lowermost soft part of the auricle is called the lobule (earlobe). Options: tragus, pyramid, concha are all parts but lobule is the lowest.选项D正确. The answer is D. The lobule is soft, non-cartilaginous.
questions.keyConcept: Lobule is the lowest soft part of the auricle - earlobe, containing fat and areolar tissue.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: In which of the following layers of the scalp does infection tend to spread:
questions.explanation: Infection tends to spread in the loose areolar connective tissue layer (layer 4) of the scalp - the 'dangerous' layer communicating with intracranial spaces.选项D正确. The answer is D. This layer lacks barriers, allowing spread.
questions.keyConcept: Loose areolar layer (layer 4) is the dangerous zone - infections spread easily to intracranial structures.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Pain from upper lip is carried by.
questions.explanation: Pain from upper lip carried by infraorbital nerve (branch of V2 maxillary division of trigeminal).选项B正确. The answer is B. This nerve exits via infraorbital foramen.
questions.keyConcept: Infraorbital nerve (V2) carries sensation from upper lip - exits at infraorbital foramen.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Infection of lateral part of the upper eye lid leads to enlargement of this group of lymph nodes:
questions.explanation: Infection of lateral part of upper eyelid drains to parotid lymph nodes (superficial parotid nodes).选项C正确. The answer is C. The medial eyelid drains to submandibular nodes.
questions.keyConcept: Lateral upper eyelid drains to parotid nodes; medial eyelid drains to submandibular nodes.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Bleeding in which layer of scalp causes black eye?
questions.explanation: Bleeding in loose areolar connective tissue layer (between aponeurosis and pericranium) causes black eye (periorbital ecchymosis) because blood tracks along this layer to the eyelid.选项D正确. The answer is D. This layer connects to the orbit.
questions.keyConcept: Loose areolar layer bleeding causes black eye - blood tracks to periorbital tissues since this layer communicates with orbit.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The nerve that carries the sensation for the lower eyelid is:
questions.explanation: The nerve that carries sensation from the lower eyelid is the infraorbital nerve (branch of V2).选项B正确. The answer is B. It supplies the lower eyelid, upper lip, and side of nose.
questions.keyConcept: Infraorbital nerve (V2) supplies the lower eyelid - part of maxillary division sensory distribution.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Regarding Scalp, all are true Except:
questions.explanation: Regarding scalp: 5 layers, vessels in connective tissue layer, infection spreads in loose areolar layer.选项C正确. The answer is C. The danger lies in layer 4 (loose areolar) connecting to intracranial venous sinuses.
questions.keyConcept: Scalp has 5 layers (SCALP) - dangerous layer is loose areolar tissue connecting to intracranial venous sinuses.
options: Its wounds gape if the aponeurosis is cut.
Its veins communicate with the intracranial venous sinuses.
It contains a muscle of facial expression.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The non-hairy region of the temple is supplied by which of the following nerves?
questions.explanation: The non-hairy region of the temple is supplied by zygomaticotemporal nerve (branch of V2 maxillary).选项D正确. The answer is D. The hairy temple is supplied by auriculotemporal nerve (V3).
questions.keyConcept: Zygomaticotemporal nerve (V2) supplies non-hairy temple; auriculotemporal (V3) supplies hairy temple.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The main sensory nerve to the lower lip is the:
questions.explanation: The main sensory nerve to the lower lip is the mental nerve (branch of inferior alveolar nerve, which is from V3).选项C正确. The answer is C. It exits via mental foramen.
questions.keyConcept: Mental nerve (V3) is the main sensory nerve to the lower lip - exits at mental foramen.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Infection of scalp area behind the ear affects which group of LNs
questions.explanation: Infection of scalp area behind the ear affects occipital lymph nodes. The scalp behind auricle drains to occipital and posterior auricular nodes.选项E正确. The answer is E. These nodes drain posterior scalp and neck.
questions.keyConcept: Posterior auricle/scalp drains to occipital and posterior auricular lymph nodes.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Which of the following is sensory to the scalp behind the auricle?
questions.explanation: The sensory nerve to the scalp behind the auricle is the greater occipital nerve (C2 dorsal ramus), NOT a trigeminal branch.选项C正确. The answer is C. It supplies from vertex to behind auricle.
questions.keyConcept: Greater occipital nerve (C2) supplies scalp behind auricle - the only non-trigeminal scalp sensory nerve.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: All of the following regarding orbicularis oris muscle is correct Except:
questions.explanation: Orbicularis oris: surrounds mouth, has no bony attachment, has multiple muscle insertions including modiolus, and is innervated by facial nerve.选项C正确. The answer is C. It closes lips and helps speech.
questions.keyConcept: Orbicularis oris: circular lip muscle, no bone attachment, facial nerve innervation - closes and purses lips.
options: It is a muscle of facial expression.
It is supplied by facial nerve.
Its fibers form complete circles around the mouth.
It can close the oral (labial) fissure.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The nerve supplying the buccinator muscle is:
questions.explanation: The nerve supplying the buccinator muscle is the buccal branch of facial nerve (NOT the buccal nerve of trigeminal which is sensory).选项B正确. The answer is B. This is a common confusion - motor to buccinator is facial nerve.
questions.keyConcept: Buccinator motor: buccal branch of facial nerve - sensory buccal nerve is V3. Common exam question!

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The following is a branch of the superficial temporal artery in the face:
questions.explanation: Superficial temporal artery (terminal branch of external carotid) gives off the transverse facial artery in the face.选项D正确. The answer is D. The transverse facial artery runs above parotid duct.
questions.keyConcept: Transverse facial artery is a branch of superficial temporal artery - runs above parotid duct in face.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The 2 frontal bellies:
questions.explanation: The two frontal bellies of occipitofrontalis: originate from skin of eyebrow, are separated by a gap (connected by Galea aponeurotica), and are supplied by supraorbital/ supratrochlear nerves.选项C正确. The answer is C. They raise eyebrows and wrinkle forehead.
questions.keyConcept: Frontal bellies of occipitofrontalis: skin of eyebrow origin, separated, raise eyebrows - supraorbital nerve supply.
options: Form the only muscle of face.
Are attached to superior temporal line.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Regarding buccinator muscle, all the following statements are true Except:
questions.explanation: Buccinator: forms cheek, pierced by parotid duct, keeps food between teeth, facial nerve motor supply.选项D正确. The answer is D. Parotid duct (Stensen's) opens opposite upper 2nd molar.
questions.keyConcept: Buccinator muscle: forms cheek, pierced by parotid duct - facial nerve motor, keeps food in dental arch.
options: It arises from both maxilla and mandible.
The pterygomandibular raphe is a common origin for this muscle and the middle constrictor.
Its middle fibers decussate at the modiolus.
It is covered by buccopharyngeal fascia.
It compresses the cheeks against the teeth.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Lacrimal part of orbicularis oculi
questions.explanation: Lacrimal part of orbicularis oculi: is attached to medial palpebral ligament, closes eye gently (orbicularis has orbital and palpebral parts).选项A正确. The answer is A. The lacrimal part specifically compresses lacrimal sac.
questions.keyConcept: Lacrimal part of orbicularis oculi attaches to medial palpebral ligament - compresses lacrimal sac.
options: Is attached to medial palpebral ligament
Is attached to lateral palpebral raphe
Is a part of orbicularis oris.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Regarding lips all are true Except:
questions.explanation: Lips: highly vascular, sensory innervation (upper V2, lower V3), motor by facial nerve, and lymph drainage varies by region.选项A正确. The answer is A. Upper lip lymph drains laterally to submandibular, medial to submental.
questions.keyConcept: Lips: V2 (upper), V3 (lower) sensation, facial nerve motor, lateral lymph drainage to submandibular.
options: The main sensory supply to upper lip is facial nerve.
The main sensory supply to lower lip is mental nerve.
Their muscles are formed mainly by orbicularis oris.
Their blood supply is through facial artery.
In facial palsy lips can’t be dilated.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The branch of facial nerve that supplies the platysma is the
questions.explanation: The branch of facial nerve that supplies the platysma is the cervical branch (also called mandibular branch in some texts).选项E正确. The answer is E. Platysma is a neck muscle of facial expression.
questions.keyConcept: Cervical branch of facial nerve supplies platysma - the only muscle in the neck from facial nerve.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Mandibular nerve is sensory to:
questions.explanation: The mandibular nerve (V3) is sensory to: lower lip, lower teeth, chin, anterior 2/3 of tongue, and cheek (via buccal nerve).选项C正确. The answer is C. It also has motor function (muscles of mastication).
questions.keyConcept: Mandibular nerve (V3): sensory to lower face/lip/teeth/tongue - also motor to mastication muscles.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Sense of movement and sense of position are lost after lesion of:
questions.explanation: Sense of movement and position (proprioception) is carried by the dorsal columns (fasciculus gracilis and cuneatus).选项D正确. The answer is D. These tracts are spared in tabes dorsalis.
questions.keyConcept: Dorsal columns carry proprioception and vibration sense - lost in dorsal column disease (tabes dorsalis).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The cuneate tract carries which of the following sensations?
questions.explanation: The cuneate tract carries sensations from the upper body (above T6): vibration, proprioception, fine touch from upper limbs and trunk.选项B正确. The answer is B. Gracile tract carries from lower body.
questions.keyConcept: Cuneate tract: upper body proprioception/vibration (above T6) - gracile carries lower body sensations.
options: Crude touch from upper & lower limbs.
Fine touch from upper & lower limbs.
Unconscious proprioception from upper and lower limbs.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: A lesion in the right gracile tract leads to loss of:
questions.explanation: Lesion in right gracile tract leads to loss of proprioception, vibration, and fine touch from the RIGHT lower limb (below T6 level).选项A正确. The answer is A. Gracile nucleus receives from lower body.
questions.keyConcept: Right gracile tract lesion: loss of proprioception/vibration from right leg - ipsilateral, below lesion level.
options: Sense of position of left big toe.
Sense of movement of right elbow joint.
Feeling of a pencil put in the right hand.
Site of touch on the right iliac fossa.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The facial colliculus overlies:
questions.explanation: The facial colliculus overlies the abducens nucleus (CN VI) and internal genu of facial nerve - located on the floor of the 4th ventricle in the pons.选项E正确. The answer is E. It's a bulge caused by these nuclei.
questions.keyConcept: Facial colliculus: overlies abducens nucleus and facial nerve genu - floor of fourth ventricle in pons.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Which of the following cerebellar parts has mainly spinal connections:
questions.explanation: The spinocerebellum (vermis and intermediate zones) has mainly spinal connections - receives proprioceptive input from spine, controls axial and limb movement.选项B正确. The answer is B. Vestibulocerebellum has vestibular connections; cerebrocerebellum has cerebral connections.
questions.keyConcept: Spinocerebellum (vermis) has spinal connections - receives proprioceptive input, controls axial muscle tone.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The cranial nerve nucleus that supplies muscles of the larynx is the:
questions.explanation: The nucleus supplying muscles of the larynx is the nucleus ambiguus - gives rise to vagus nerve (CN X) which innervates most laryngeal muscles.选项B正确. The answer is B. The recurrent laryngeal nerve comes from vagus.
questions.keyConcept: Nucleus ambiguus (vagus) innervates laryngeal muscles via recurrent laryngeal nerve - voice production.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The left spinal lemniscus carries sensations of:
questions.explanation: The left spinal lemniscus carries sensations from the RIGHT side of the body (because it has already crossed in the medulla/spinal cord).选项B正确. The answer is B. The spinothalamic tract crosses at spinal cord level.
questions.keyConcept: Left spinal lemniscus carries right-sided pain/temperature - spinothalamic tract crosses at cord level.
options: Pain from the left side of the body.
Conscious proprioception from the left side of the body.
Muscle tone from right side of the body.
Crude touch from the right side of the body.
Fine touch from right side of body.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Hemisection of spinal cord gives the following symptoms on the same side below the level of lesion:
questions.explanation: Brown-Sequard syndrome (hemisection of spinal cord): ipsilateral motor weakness and proprioception loss (corticospinal and dorsal columns) BELOW lesion; contralateral pain/temperature loss (spinothalamic) 1-2 segments below lesion.选项D正确. The answer is D. This is the classic dissociated sensory loss pattern.
questions.keyConcept: Brown-Sequard: ipsilateral motor/ proprioception loss, contralateral pain/temperature loss - below lesion level.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Rootlets of glossopharyngeal nerve lie:
questions.explanation: Rootlets of glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX) lie in the postolivary sulcus, between the olive and inferior cerebellar peduncle in the medulla.选项B正确. The answer is B. They emerge as 3-4 rootlets.
questions.keyConcept: CN IX rootlets emerge in postolivary sulcus of medulla - between olive and inferior cerebellar peduncle.
options: Between olive and inferior cerebellar peduncle
Between lower border of pons and medulla

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The inferior cerebellar peduncle contains:
questions.explanation: The inferior cerebellar peduncle contains: dorsal spinocerebellar tract (carries proprioceptive info to cerebellum), and vestibular connections.选项D正确. The answer is D. It carries afferent and efferent cerebellar pathways.
questions.keyConcept: Inferior cerebellar peduncle: dorsal spinocerebellar tract + vestibular connections - afferent to cerebellum.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: General visceral efferent column includes the following nuclei Except:
questions.explanation: General visceral efferent column includes: dorsal motor nucleus of vagus, inferior salivatory nucleus, and superior salivatory nucleus. The Edinger-Westphal is parasympathetic to eye, NOT included here.选项C正确. The answer is C. Edinger-Westphal is for eye, not for glands/viscera.
questions.keyConcept: GVE column: dorsal vagal, inferior and superior salivatory nuclei - NOT Edinger-Westphal (eye).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Special visceral efferent nuclei include:
questions.explanation: Special visceral efferent nuclei include: trigeminal motor nucleus (V), facial motor nucleus (VII), nucleus ambiguus (IX, X, XI), and hypoglossal nucleus (XII).选项D正确. The answer is D. These innervate pharyngeal arch-derived muscles.
questions.keyConcept: Special visceral efferent nuclei: CN V, VII, IX, X, XI motor nuclei - innervate pharyngeal arch muscles.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Which of the following nuclei represents the somatic efferent column?
questions.explanation: The somatic efferent column includes: oculomotor (III), trochlear (IV), abducens (VI), and hypoglossal (XII) nuclei - these control extraocular and tongue muscles.选项A正确. The answer is A. These are all somatic motor nuclei.
questions.keyConcept: Somatic efferent column: CN III, IV, VI, XII - control eye muscles and tongue muscles.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: All the following are nuclei of facial nerve EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Facial nerve nuclei include: facial motor nucleus (muscles of expression), superior salivatory nucleus (parasympathetic lacrimal/nasal glands), and solitary nucleus (taste from anterior 2/3 tongue). The cochlear nucleus is for hearing, NOT part of facial nerve.选项D正确. The answer is D. Cochlear nucleus is CN VIII.
questions.keyConcept: Facial nerve nuclei: motor (expression), superior salivatory (lacrimal), solitary (taste) - NOT cochlear nucleus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The nucleus that receives taste fibers is:
questions.explanation: The nucleus that receives taste fibers is the solitary nucleus (nucleus tractus solitarius) - receives taste from CN VII, IX, X.选项A正确. The answer is A. Located in medulla.
questions.keyConcept: Solitary nucleus receives taste: CN VII (anterior 2/3 tongue), CN IX (posterior 1/3), CN X (epiglottis).

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The falx cerebri:
questions.explanation: The falx cerebri: a dura mater fold between cerebral hemispheres, attached to crista galli anteriorly and tentorium posteriorly, contains superior sagittal sinus.选项B正确. The answer is B. It prevents hemisphere displacement.
questions.keyConcept: Falx cerebri: dura fold between hemispheres, contains superior sagittal sinus - prevents midline shift.
options: Is attached anteriorly to anterior clinoid process.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Extradural hemorrhage is caused by rupture of:
questions.explanation: Extradural hemorrhage caused by rupture of middle meningeal artery (usually from temporal bone fracture).选项C正确. The answer is C. This is a surgical emergency - lucid interval then rapid deterioration.
questions.keyConcept: Extradural hematoma: middle meningeal artery rupture - 'talk and die' syndrome, biconvex shape on CT.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Regarding pituitary gland, all the following statements are true Except:
questions.explanation: Pituitary gland: in sella turcica, connected to hypothalamus via infundibulum, anterior lobe (adenohypophysis) and posterior lobe (neurohypophysis), has portal circulation.选项A正确. The answer is A. Portal system allows hypothalamic regulation.
questions.keyConcept: Pituitary: sella turcica, two lobes, portal circulation for hypothalamic control - posterior stores ADH/oxytocin.
options: It lies in anterior part of the neck.
It has a portal system of veins.
Axons of nerve cells in hypothalamus carry hormones to the neurohypophysis.
The adenohypophysis secretes at least six different hormones.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: All are contents of infratemporal fossa Except:
questions.explanation: Infratemporal fossa contents: lateral pterygoid, medial pterygoid, maxillary artery, pterygoid venous plexus, mandibular nerve, otic ganglion.选项E正确. The answer is E. The pterygoid muscles and vessels are key contents.
questions.keyConcept: Infratemporal fossa: pterygoid muscles, maxillary artery, mandibular nerve, otic ganglion - NOT the orbit.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: A muscle attached to the coronoid process of mandible:
questions.explanation: Muscle attached to coronoid process of mandible: temporalis (and lateral pterygoid attaches to condylar neck and articular disc).选项D正确. The answer is D. Temporalis inserts on coronoid process and anterior mandibular ramus.
questions.keyConcept: Temporalis muscle inserts on coronoid process of mandible - elevation and retraction of mandible.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The buccal branch of the mandibular nerve supplies:
questions.explanation: The buccal branch of mandibular nerve (V3) supplies: motor to lateral pterygoid, and sensory to cheek (buccal mucosa, skin over buccinator).选项B正确. The answer is B. This is sensory to cheek, NOT motor to buccinator.
questions.keyConcept: Buccal nerve (V3): sensory to cheek mucosa/skin - motor to lateral pterygoid, NOT buccinator.
options: Skin and mucous membrane of cheek.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The otic ganglion:
questions.explanation: Otic ganglion: parasympathetic ganglion near foramen ovale, receives fibers from lesser petrosal nerve (CN IX), sends postganglionic to parotid gland.选项E正确. The answer is E. It is suspended from V3.
questions.keyConcept: Otic ganglion: parasympathetic to parotid - receives CN IX via lesser petrosal, suspended from V3.
options: Lies deep to the mandibular nerve.
Is functionally connected to the glossopharyngeal nerve.
Is closely related to the nerve to the medial pterygoid muscle.
Its sympathetic root is derived from the plexus around internal carotid artery.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Regarding the mandibular nerve, all are true Except:
questions.explanation: Mandibular nerve (V3) carries: sensory to face/teeth/tongue, motor to mastication muscles.选项D正确. The answer is D. It exits foramen ovale.
questions.keyConcept: Mandibular nerve (V3): sensory to face/teeth/tongue + motor to muscles of mastication - exits foramen ovale.
options: It supplies all lower jaw teeth.
It has motor and sensory fibers.
It passes in lateral wall of cavernous sinus.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: The lingual nerve:
questions.explanation: Lingual nerve (V3): carries general sensation from anterior 2/3 tongue, runs lateral to hyoglossus muscle, carries chorda tympani (taste) fibers.选项E正确. The answer is E. It runs close to third molar roots.
questions.keyConcept: Lingual nerve (V3): general sensation anterior 2/3 tongue + taste (via chorda tympani) - runs near hyoglossus.
options: Is a branch of the posterior division of maxillary nerve.
Carries fibers from first cervical spinal nerve.
Carries taste from posterior third of tongue.
Is closely related to the third molar tooth.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: A lesion of mandibular nerve immediately after its exit from foramen oval may lead to:
questions.explanation: Lesion of mandibular nerve immediately after foramen ovale causes: sensory loss in face/teeth/tongue, motor loss in muscles of mastication, and paralysis of tensor tympani/stapedius.选项E正确. The answer is E. All functions of V3 would be lost.
questions.keyConcept: Foramen ovale V3 lesion: loss of facial sensation, mastication muscles, tensor tympani - complete V3 deficit.
options: Loss of taste sensation from anterior part of tongue.
Loss of general sensations from posterior part of tongue.
Loss of sensation of lower lip.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Injury of motor root of trigeminal nerve would cause paralysis of:
questions.explanation: Injury of motor root of trigeminal nerve (portio minor) would cause paralysis of: muscles of mastication (masseter, temporalis, medial and lateral pterygoids), mylohyoid, anterior belly of digastric, tensor tympani, tensor veli palatini.选项B正确. The answer is B. These are all innervated by CN V3 motor root.
questions.keyConcept: Motor root of CN V: mastication muscles, mylohyoid, digastric, tensor tympani/veli palatini - all affected.

questions.subject: Anatomy
questions.text: Regarding chorda tympani; all are correct statements Except:
questions.explanation: Chorda tympani: carries taste from anterior 2/3 tongue (via lingual nerve), carries parasympathetic to submandibular and sublingual glands, crosses middle ear, joins lingual nerve.选项C正确. The answer is C. It does NOT supply the tongue directly - runs with lingual nerve.
questions.keyConcept: Chorda tympani: taste + parasympathetic to submandibular/sublingual - runs with lingual nerve to tongue.
options: It is a branch of facial nerve.
It joins lingual nerve deep to lateral pterygoid.
It is related to medial side of lower third molar.
